overview: The School Committee approved a major expansion and restructuring of the district's after-school programs and renewed the superintendent's contract for three years. The committee also voted to support state legislation resolving pension discrepancies for veteran educators.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: Approved various budget transfers, a $700 PTO donation to the Fine Arts and Music program, and previous meeting minutes.

items.title: Mustang Moment: World Language and English Learning
items.summary: Students from the World Language and English Learning departments shared personal testimonials regarding the value of biliteracy and cultural exchange.

items.title: Mustang Moment: Brooks Elementary Songwriting Project
items.summary: Third-grade students performed an original song about Medford's history and future created during a 10-year recurring creative writing residency.

items.title: After School Program Review and Recommendations
items.summary: Approved a comprehensive plan to increase enrollment capacity by 150 seats, establish full-time site directors, and implement specialist-led enrichment activities. The reform addresses high waitlists and creates a more structured, multi-age programming model across elementary sites.

items.title: MPS After School Rate Card
items.summary: Approved a new tuition rate card featuring flexible daily scheduling and a rate increase of approximately 10% to fund expanded staffing and benefits.

items.title: Superintendent's Three-Year Contract
items.summary: Approved a three-year contract for Superintendent Suzanne Galusi following executive session negotiations.

items.title: Resolution Supporting Teacher Retirement Benefits
items.summary: Approved a resolution endorsing Massachusetts House Bill H.4361 and Senate Bill S.1884 to provide a one-time pension buy-in opportunity for veteran teachers affected by previous administrative errors.

items.title: Condolences and Adjournment
items.summary: Offered condolences to the family of Leonard Len Gliona and announced upcoming budget hearings before adjourning.
